claims.text: The disputed SGD 3.20 line is for the Bukit Merah Central westbound gantry, and the platform's own derived ERP proximity check places the vehicle's nearest GPS fix 7,482.07 m from those gantry coordinates. That is roughly thirty times outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 applies, and the derived block reports gap_brackets_closest_approach as false with no bracketing gaps: the trace does not cross this gantry on any reading. The line is therefore a charge for a gantry the trace never passes, refundable in full as a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), available whether or not any deviation exists.

Nothing in the contemporaneous record supports the crossing, and both parties' accounts are consistent with it never having happened. The driver's own counterparty statement on file concedes he 'did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt', and the rider's only chat message is a query about that same ERP line. Read with the derived proximity figure of 7,482.07 m, the SGD 3.20 line has no evidentiary basis and cannot stand.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: quoted_fare_sgd is SGD 22.00 and the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so under POL-RD-11 the rider is already whole on those lines and POL-RD-02 does not run. What POL-RD-11(a) leaves the rider is the amount by which charged_total (SGD 25.20) exceeds quoted_fare (SGD 22.00) plus pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only ERP gantry on the fare is flagged on_optimal_route false and was never crossed, so properly chargeable pass-throughs are SGD 0.00 and the whole SGD 3.20 excess is refundable.

The contested amount is SGD 3.20 and the whole of it falls away. Under POL-GEN-03 FULL_REFUND is the return of the entire contested amount to the filing party, and that is exactly what POL-RD-09(4) produces here, so the rider should be recorded as entirely right on the contested sum rather than as a partial winner.

The no-crossing finding is read off a clean, unimpaired trace rather than inferred from a hole in it. The GPS artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, covering 100% of the trip with 169 fixes at a 10-second interval and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, and the derived gantry block shows no bracketing gaps and gap_brackets_closest_approach false. POL-RD-07 has no purchase: there is no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds, so no trace-impairment argument is open against this conclusion.

POL-RD-01 establishes the deviation on this trip's own trace: 16.0 km of trace distance against a 12.5 km optimal is a 3.5 km excess, 28.0% of optimal, clearing both the 20% and the 0.8 km limbs. The excess is not MATERIAL (below 50% and below 8.0 km), and on an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip POL-RD-11 still closes the distance-refund route, so this limb moves no money. It matters because it confirms the vehicle was off the optimal corridor and yet the derived check still puts it 7.5 km from the charged gantry — that gantry lies on neither the optimal route nor the route actually driven.

No exoneration is available to the driver on the deviation: the traffic advisory artifact is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), and I disclose that impairment. An absent advisory cannot satisfy POL-RD-03(a), which requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses with an overlapping validity window, so nothing reduces the rider's position on that footing.

Escalation under POL-RD-10 is not engaged. The single unmatched charge line is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), and POL-RD-09 expressly provides that POL-RD-10(8) is not triggered where the only unmatched line is one refunded under that limb. The refund of SGD 3.20 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6), the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip TRP-09114, and the deciding artifacts sit at weight 1.0, well above the 0.70 floor.

Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess — the detour cost falls on the driver, not the rider. The rider's remedies are confined to the pass-through and statutory lines, so the route-deviation framing cannot yield a fare refund; the single live question is the one SGD 3.20 pass-through line.

The trace measures 16.0 km against a 12.5 km optimal route, an excess of 3.5 km or 28.00%. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km) but does not reach the materiality gate (over 50% or over 8.0 km), so this is not a MATERIAL deviation. The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is therefore never engaged, and no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral can attach to this trip.

Even if the driver_profile is consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610. Neither limb of the POL-RD-06 pattern test is satisfied — there are not three flags in 90 days, and the flag rate is 0.00, far below the 0.05 threshold — so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and the rider's remedy cannot be uplifted on any pattern basis.

The gps_trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 169 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. None of the POL-RD-07(a)-(c) limbs fires, so the trace may be relied on directly, and none of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers — in particular the impaired-trace trigger at POL-RD-10(3) — is engaged; the dispute is fully decidable on this record without a human reviewer.

The rider's recovery is capped at the single ERP line. The fare_breakdown carries one gantry charge — SGD 3.20 for Bukit Merah Central westbound — and the derived gantry proximity places the nearest trace fix 7482 m from that gantry, far outside the 250 m match radius in POL-RD-09. The driver accepts that this one line is a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), and that POL-RD-11(a) returns the amount by which charged_total of SGD 25.20 exceeds the SGD 22.00 quote; but that is the whole of it, it is a fare-correction matter and not a driver-conduct finding, and no sum beyond SGD 3.20 is payable on this record.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the rider's claim is allowed in full and SGD 3.20 is refunded.

WHAT IS AGREED. This was an upfront-quoted trip (EV-FARE-09114, fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE): SGD 22.00 quoted, SGD 25.20 charged, the SGD 3.20 difference being a single pass-through line for the 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP gantry.

The upfront-pricing point is accepted. Because the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE, POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so the deviation shown on the trace earns no distance-or-time refund however large it is. The rider's threshold arguments are accepted but move no money: POL-RD-01 is satisfied on this trip's own trace (16.0 km against a 12.5 km optimal — 3.5 km excess, 28.0%, over both the 20% and 0.8 km gates), but the excess is not MATERIAL (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged on materiality; and even if the profile were consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct referral attaches. This is a fare-correction matter, not a conduct finding.

THE ERP LINE CANNOT STAND. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-09114) is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, covering the whole trip with 169 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage and no gaps. Its derived proximity check places the vehicle's nearest fix 7,482.07 m from the charged gantry's coordinates — roughly thirty times outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 applies — with no bracketing gaps and gap_brackets_closest_approach false; the line is also flagged on_optimal_route false. The vehicle never passed the gantry, so the SGD 3.20 is a charge for a gantry the trace never crossed: a phantom line refundable in full as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4), available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver's own statement — 'The route was longer than expected, but I did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt' — is an admission against interest and agrees with the trace. It carries no weight multiplier, so it neither raises nor lowers the confidence cap; it is simply consistent corroboration.

NO ESCALATION. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes (no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 s), so the no-crossing finding rests on a clean instrument. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown; no timestamps conflict; the only fare line without a counterpart anywhere in the trace is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes; the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling; and confidence is well above the 0.70 floor. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09114-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT). It is cited only to note that no POL-RD-03 exoneration is available to the driver; nothing in this ruling decides any fact on it, so it neither caps confidence nor triggers escalation, and POL-RD-03 would in any event only have excused the deviation, which already moves no money under POL-RD-11.

OUTCOME. The whole contested amount of SGD 3.20 is returned to the rider, so the ruling is FULL_REFUND. The GPS trace and the fare breakdown, both at weight 1.0, carry the deciding fact. The billing-integrity referral below records the phantom line for the platform's records and neither delays nor displaces the refund.

To both parties. Two questions run through this case and they come out differently.

The route. This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: the fare_breakdown records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd 22.00. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-09114, weight 1.0) is complete and unimpaired — 169 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps — and it runs 16.0 km against the 12.5 km optimal stored on the trip record, an excess of 3.5 km or 28.0%. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is established, but it does not reach the materiality gate (over 50% or over 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 pattern check in the uplift sense is engaged. More importantly, on an upfront-quoted fare POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, the rider is already whole on those lines, and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The detour cost sits with the driver. The POL-RD-06 consult is anyway academic: the driver_profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610, so neither limb of the pattern test is met and no conduct referral attaches.

The SGD 3.20. This is the whole of the contested amount and the whole of what is returned. It is an ERP line for the Bukit Merah Central westbound gantry. The platform's own derived proximity check, read off the clean trace, places the vehicle's nearest fix 7,482.07 m from those gantry coordinates — roughly thirty times outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 applies — with gap_brackets_closest_approach false and no bracketing gaps. The trace does not cross that gantry on any reading. The driver's own statement on file agrees he 'did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt', and the rider's only chat message queries that same line. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refundable in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists. Because the entire contested amount is returned, the outcome is FULL_REFUND.

The two routes to this money — POL-RD-09(4) and the POL-RD-11(a) over-quote figure — are the same SGD 3.20 and are not added together; the refund is counted once.

Driver: no adverse conduct finding is made against you. The outcome turns on a phantom ERP charge, not on your driving, and your record shows no trailing-window deviation flags.

No escalation is required. The trip identifiers on the trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown all match TRP-09114; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c); the deciding artifacts sit at weight 1.0, above the 0.70 floor; and the only unmatched charge line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-09 expressly excludes from POL-RD-10(8). The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09114-01, weight 0.0) is not relied on by either side to excuse the deviation, and the deviation moves no money in any event, so its absence does not bear on the outcome.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 3.20 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP line on fare_breakdown EV-FARE-09114 was charged for a gantry the GPS trace never crosses (nearest fix 7,482.07 m away against a 250 m match radius; no bracketing approach), and has been refunded in full as an unmatched phantom charge. Record as a billing-integrity finding against the charged line.

ruling.explanation:
This was an upfront-quoted trip (SGD 22.00) and the only sum in dispute is the separate SGD 3.20 ERP line for the Bukit Merah Central westbound gantry. That line cannot stand, and the whole contested SGD 3.20 is returned.

To the rider: you are right about the ERP line. The GPS trace for this trip is complete and unimpaired — 169 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds — and the platform's own proximity check puts the car's nearest fix 7,482 m from the gantry, roughly thirty times outside the 250 m radius POL-RD-09 uses to treat a gantry as crossed. The derived block reports no bracketing gaps and gap_brackets_closest_approach false, and the fare_breakdown itself flags the gantry as on_optimal_route false. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full. Independently, POL-RD-11(a) returns the amount by which charged_total (SGD 25.20) exceeds the quote (SGD 22.00) plus properly chargeable pass-throughs (SGD 0.00), which is the same SGD 3.20. This is one correction of SGD 3.20, not two: POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule keeps it from being added on top of anything else, and POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront fare, so no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. You are therefore recorded as entirely right on the contested amount.

To the driver: your account that you did not see or pass the gantry is consistent with the trace and supports the finding, but the deciding fact is carried by the GPS trace and fare_breakdown, both at weight 1.0. What the trace shows beyond the gantry does not change the money. The route was measured at 16.0 km against a 12.5 km optimal — an established excess of 3.5 km, 28.0%, clearing the POL-RD-01 gate — but on an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking and no distance refund is available however large the excess. The excess is also below the materiality gate (50% or 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not required; in any event deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days, no repeat pattern is established, and no conduct referral attaches. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-09114-01, weight 0.0) is not held against you: it could only have exculpated, it rests on no field, and its absence carries no fact.

Escalation is not engaged. The single unmatched charge line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), and POL-RD-09 expressly provides that POL-RD-10(8) is not triggered where the only unmatched line is refunded under that limb; the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling; trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; and the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c).

The SGD 3.20 is refunded in full (amount already a multiple of SGD 0.05), and the billing-integrity finding is referred as set out above.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 3.20 ERP charge for the 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' gantry is refunded in full as a phantom line — the GPS trace's nearest fix lies 7,482 m from the gantry, far outside the 250 m crossing radius, and the gantry is flagged on_optimal_route false.

ledger.claim: The disputed SGD 3.20 line is for the Bukit Merah Central westbound gantry, and the platform's own derived ERP proximity check places the vehicle's nearest GPS fix 7,482.07 m from those gantry coordinates. That is roughly thirty times outside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 applies, and the derived block reports gap_brackets_closest_approach as false with no bracketing gaps: the trace does not cross this gantry on any reading. The line is therefore a charge for a gantry the trace never passes, refundable in full as a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), available whether or not any deviation exists.

Nothing in the contemporaneous record supports the crossing, and both parties' accounts are consistent with it never having happened. The driver's own counterparty statement on file concedes he 'did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt', and the rider's only chat message is a query about that same ERP line. Read with the derived proximity figure of 7,482.07 m, the SGD 3.20 line has no evidentiary basis and cannot stand.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: quoted_fare_sgd is SGD 22.00 and the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so under POL-RD-11 the rider is already whole on those lines and POL-RD-02 does not run. What POL-RD-11(a) leaves the rider is the amount by which charged_total (SGD 25.20) exceeds quoted_fare (SGD 22.00) plus pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only ERP gantry on the fare is flagged on_optimal_route false and was never crossed, so properly chargeable pass-throughs are SGD 0.00 and the whole SGD 3.20 excess is refundable.

The contested amount is SGD 3.20 and the whole of it falls away. Under POL-GEN-03 FULL_REFUND is the return of the entire contested amount to the filing party, and that is exactly what POL-RD-09(4) produces here, so the rider should be recorded as entirely right on the contested sum rather than as a partial winner.

The no-crossing finding is read off a clean, unimpaired trace rather than inferred from a hole in it. The GPS artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, covering 100% of the trip with 169 fixes at a 10-second interval and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, and the derived gantry block shows no bracketing gaps and gap_brackets_closest_approach false. POL-RD-07 has no purchase: there is no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds, so no trace-impairment argument is open against this conclusion.

POL-RD-01 establishes the deviation on this trip's own trace: 16.0 km of trace distance against a 12.5 km optimal is a 3.5 km excess, 28.0% of optimal, clearing both the 20% and the 0.8 km limbs. The excess is not MATERIAL (below 50% and below 8.0 km), and on an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip POL-RD-11 still closes the distance-refund route, so this limb moves no money. It matters because it confirms the vehicle was off the optimal corridor and yet the derived check still puts it 7.5 km from the charged gantry — that gantry lies on neither the optimal route nor the route actually driven.

No exoneration is available to the driver on the deviation: the traffic advisory artifact is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), and I disclose that impairment. An absent advisory cannot satisfy POL-RD-03(a), which requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses with an overlapping validity window, so nothing reduces the rider's position on that footing.

Escalation under POL-RD-10 is not engaged. The single unmatched charge line is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), and POL-RD-09 expressly provides that POL-RD-10(8) is not triggered where the only unmatched line is one refunded under that limb. The refund of SGD 3.20 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6), the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip TRP-09114, and the deciding artifacts sit at weight 1.0, well above the 0.70 floor.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: the fare_breakdown records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 22.00 and charged_total 25.20. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess — the detour cost falls on the driver, not the rider. The rider's remedies are confined to the pass-through and statutory lines, so the route-deviation framing cannot yield a fare refund; the single live question is the one SGD 3.20 pass-through line.

The trace measures 16.0 km against a 12.5 km optimal route, an excess of 3.5 km or 28.00%. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km) but does not reach the materiality gate (over 50% or over 8.0 km), so this is not a MATERIAL deviation. The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is therefore never engaged, and no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral can attach to this trip.

Even if the driver_profile is consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610. Neither limb of the POL-RD-06 pattern test is satisfied — there are not three flags in 90 days, and the flag rate is 0.00, far below the 0.05 threshold — so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and the rider's remedy cannot be uplifted on any pattern basis.

The gps_trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 169 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. None of the POL-RD-07(a)-(c) limbs fires, so the trace may be relied on directly, and none of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers — in particular the impaired-trace trigger at POL-RD-10(3) — is engaged; the dispute is fully decidable on this record without a human reviewer.

The rider's recovery is capped at the single ERP line. The fare_breakdown carries one gantry charge — SGD 3.20 for Bukit Merah Central westbound — and the derived gantry proximity places the nearest trace fix 7482 m from that gantry, far outside the 250 m match radius in POL-RD-09. The driver accepts that this one line is a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), and that POL-RD-11(a) returns the amount by which charged_total of SGD 25.20 exceeds the SGD 22.00 quote; but that is the whole of it, it is a fare-correction matter and not a driver-conduct finding, and no sum beyond SGD 3.20 is payable on this record.
